nodes.summary: For a nonempty finite set $\alpha$ and a natural number $q$, the collision experiment is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ obtained by drawing a function $s \colon \{0, \dots, q - 1\} \to \alpha$ uniformly at random (equivalently, $q$ independent uniform samples $s(0), \dots, s(q - 1)$ from $\alpha$) and outputting true exactly when $s$ is not injective, that is, when $s(i) = s(j)$…
nodes.title: The collision experiment

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision equals $1 - N (N - 1) \cdots (N - q + 1) / N^q$, where the product $N (N - 1) \cdots (N - q + 1)$ has $q$ factors (it is $1$ for $q = 0$ and $0$ for $q > N$).
nodes.title: The exact collision probability

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q \le \sqrt{N}$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.
nodes.title: Birthday lower bound for at most square-root many samples

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q \le \sqrt{2 N}$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.
nodes.title: Birthday lower bound as stated in Katz and Lindell

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q (q - 1) \le 2 N$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.
nodes.title: Birthday lower bound

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at most $q (q - 1) / (2 N)$.
nodes.title: Birthday upper bound

nodes.summary: For a nonempty finite set $\alpha$ and a natural number $q$, the collision probability is the probability, as a real number, that the collision experiment with $q$ samples from $\alpha$ outputs true, that is, that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain two equal samples at distinct positions.
nodes.title: Collision probability

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements, $q$ a natural number, and $x = q (q - 1) / (2 N)$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $x / (1 + x)$.
nodes.title: Birthday lower bound, rational form

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $2 N \le q (q - 1)$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $1/2$.
nodes.title: Even odds of a collision

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $1 - \exp(-q (q - 1) / (2 N))$.
nodes.title: Birthday lower bound, exponential form

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
